scientific_question: Does source-transfer contrast collapse on exact response direction when that direction is changed by two physically different routes?

common_controls.target_mode_energy: exactly equal for all 16 modes by prospective drive-variance weighting
common_controls.source_P_relation: screening-aligned: same lambda as target, changed aspect ratio
common_controls.source_G_relation: aspect-aligned: same aspect ratio as target, changed lambda

route_A_screening.description: Keep boundary-mode support fixed at 1-8 and 17-24; change target screening.

route_B_excitation_support.description: Keep target screening fixed at pi; shift one contiguous 16-mode boundary band upward.

registered_rivals.response_direction: After accounting for exact bandwise distance and the small residual angle mismatch, normalized source contrast agrees across the two routes and weakens as the response directions converge.
registered_rivals.screening_regime: Matched-angle pairs differ systematically because changing lambda alters propagation in a way response angle does not capture.
registered_rivals.excitation_support: Matched-angle pairs differ systematically because the boundary-frequency support carries information not captured by response angle.
registered_rivals.categorical_screening_alignment: P wins both mode halves across both routes.
registered_rivals.categorical_aspect_alignment: G wins both mode halves across both routes.
registered_rivals.learner_specificity: The paired pattern reverses across prospectively declared learner classes.

outcomes.primary: Paired-route difference in the signed, band-resolved P-versus-G target-error contrast, reported beside each route's exact minimum-change null.
secondary: source contrast versus exact source-source chord
aggregate deviation from the exact P/G tie
target-only and linear-reconstruction fidelity in every route
outcomes.interpretation: Agreement across routes supports response direction; a route-specific residual supports the corresponding global-regime or excitation-support account.

validity_gates: Every target must retain 16 equal-energy response modes and every source must remain exactly 15% from its target.
The source P/G total-distance tie and opposite-half distance crossover must hold before learning.
A route comparison is invalid if target-only or exact-linear-reference fidelity differs enough to explain the source contrast.
No architecture-robust claim is permitted from one learner class.
The paired angles are close, not identical; exact angle and chord remain covariates rather than being rounded into categorical bins.

rejected_observation_measure_route.reason: Changing where the same target field was observed produced little clean rotation. Achieving a material angle change required extreme target drive reweighting.
rejected_observation_measure_route.example: A far-interior exponential observation density with rate 16 reduced the angle to about 37.9 degrees but required a target drive-variance dynamic range of about 9.2e3.
rejected_observation_measure_route.decision: Do not use observation weighting as the second causal route.

numerical_verification.method: Closed-form modal responses, equal-energy drive weights, Gauss-Legendre quadrature, and scalar root solves for equal-radius sources.

scope_limits: Both routes remain within one separable screened elliptic family.
Higher mode support creates thinner excitation-driven spatial structure even though the PDE screening stays fixed.
A positive paired result would justify testing response direction on a nonseparable geometry; it would not yet establish a universal transfer law.
